title: Advance Rulings
outcomes: Explain advance rulings and eligible applicants.
Describe the BAR and the application process.
Apply provisions on void rulings and appeals.

meta.exam_tip: Test applicant category, exclusions and fee before discussing procedure.

concepts.title: Meaning of advance ruling and eligible applicants
body: An advance ruling (section 380(a)) is a determination by the Board for Advance Rulings on a question of law or fact about (i) a transaction undertaken or proposed by a non-resident; (ii) a resident's transaction with a non-resident, regarding the non-resident's liability; (iii) a resident's own transactions of ₹100 crore or more; (iv) a notified resident's (public sector company's) pending issue of income computation; or (v) whether an arrangement proposed by any person is an impermissible avoidance arrangement under GAAR.
The applicant must fall in one of these categories; residents below the ₹100 crore threshold (other than public sector companies and GAAR questions) cannot apply.
Advance rulings provide certainty before a transaction and reduce litigation, especially for cross-border structures.
concepts.analogy: Certainty upfront for significant or cross-border transactions.
concepts.work: A non-resident planning to sell shares of an Indian company can seek a ruling on taxability.

concepts.title: Board for Advance Rulings and application
body: Section 381: the Central Government constitutes Boards for Advance Rulings, each with two members not below the rank of Chief Commissioner. Proceedings are not invalid merely because of a vacancy or defect in constitution (section 382).

Section 383: application in the prescribed form, stating the question, with fees under Rule 200 — for non-resident transactions, ₹2 lakh (under ₹100 crore), ₹5 lakh (₹100–300 crore) and ₹10 lakh (above ₹300 crore); for resident transactions, ₹5 lakh (₹100–300 crore) and ₹10 lakh (above ₹300 crore); ₹10,000 in other cases.
An application may be withdrawn within 30 days from the date of application.
concepts.analogy: Two senior members; fees scale with transaction size.
concepts.work: A ₹250 crore non-resident transaction requires a fee of ₹5 lakh.

concepts.title: Procedure, exclusions and pronouncement
body: Section 384: the BAR sends a copy of the application to the PCIT/CIT and calls for records. It may allow or reject the application but cannot allow it where the question is already pending before an income-tax authority, the Tribunal or a court (except for notified public sector companies), involves determination of fair market value of property, or relates to a transaction or issue designed prima facie for avoidance of tax (except a GAAR determination).

No application is rejected without hearing, and reasons are recorded. If allowed, the BAR examines further material and pronounces its ruling within six months of receipt, giving a hearing if requested (through an authorised representative if desired).
Signed copies of the ruling go to the applicant and the PCIT/CIT. The BAR has civil-court powers and regulates its own procedure (sections 387, 388).
concepts.analogy: Pending, valuation and avoidance questions are kept out.
concepts.work: A question already before the CIT(A) cannot be taken to the BAR.

concepts.title: Void rulings and appeal
body: Section 386: if the BAR finds, on its own or on representation of the PCIT/CIT or applicant, that a ruling was obtained by fraud or misrepresentation of facts, it may declare the ruling void ab initio ; the Act then applies as if no ruling had been made.

When the Act is applied after a void ruling, the period from the date of the ruling to the date of the order declaring it void is excluded. The BAR may also rectify mistakes apparent from the record before the AO gives effect to a ruling.
Section 389: the applicant or the PCIT/CIT may appeal to the jurisdictional High Court within 60 days of communication of the ruling or order (condonable for sufficient cause).
concepts.analogy: Fraud voids a ruling; appeals go straight to the High Court.
concepts.work: A ruling based on suppressed facts can be declared void from the start.

viva.q: Can a public sector company seek a ruling on a pending issue?
viva.model: Yes, as a notified resident it may apply even if the question is pending before an income-tax authority or the Tribunal.

viva.q: What happens to limitation after a ruling is declared void?
viva.model: The period from the date of the ruling to the order declaring it void is excluded when applying the time limits.

viva.q: Who receives a copy of the ruling?
viva.model: The applicant and the PCIT or CIT concerned.

viva.q: Can GAAR questions be referred to the BAR?
viva.model: Yes, any person may seek a determination whether a proposed arrangement is an impermissible avoidance arrangement.

viva.q: Does a vacancy in the BAR invalidate its ruling?
viva.model: Proceedings remain valid despite a vacancy or defect in its constitution.
